meta.title: Flagline: Heat Safety For Every Outdoor Practice
meta.description: Free WBGT and smoke safety for Texas school athletics and marching band. Plan the session, run the 30-minute rechecks and keep the UIL record.

home.heroTitle: Heat Rules, Handled On The Sideline.
home.heroLead: Free WBGT and smoke safety for every outdoor practice in Texas. Plan the session, run the 30-minute rechecks and keep the record your athletic director needs.
home.themeLine: Built for WarriorHacks 2.0: an issue in our community, county, state and nation.
home.ruleLine: Since August 1, 2026, Texas UIL requires WBGT monitoring for every outdoor athletic practice and marching band rehearsal.
home.sourcesTitle: Built On Official Rules And Open Data
home.bentoTitle: One Tool For The Whole Practice.
home.bentoLead: From the night before to the signed log, Flagline turns the UIL chart into a plan your staff can follow in five seconds.
home.planBody: Hour by hour flags for the next week, from two independent forecasts. Find the window where practice can run in full.
home.runBody: Practice Mode counts down to every required reading, schedules the breaks and updates the rules the moment the level rises.
home.protectBody: Athletes check in privately. Red flags reach the trainer instantly, and the heat stroke protocol is one tap away.
home.proveBody: Every reading, break and change is recorded into a signed, bilingual practice log for the athletic director.
home.statsLead: Exertional heat stroke is the leading preventable cause of death in high school football. It is also almost always survivable when cooling starts within minutes.
home.stat1Label: Heat illnesses among US high school athletes each year (CDC)
home.stat2Label: Between required WBGT readings during practice (UIL)
home.stat3Label: Independent forecasts behind every number we show
home.stat4Label: For every school, coach and athlete
home.howLead: Deterministic rules for anything safety critical. Calibrated AI only where plain words need to become typed facts.
home.step1Body: We compute WBGT with the Liljegren physics model on Open-Meteo data and compare it with the National Weather Service forecast. The flag always uses the higher one.
home.step2Title: The UIL Chart, As Tested Code
home.step2Body: Class 2 and Class 3 thresholds, break rules, football gear and the red flag conditioning ban are versioned data with hundreds of conformance tests.
home.step3Body: Forecasts plan the day. On the field, Flagline asks for a reading before practice and every 30 minutes, and the measured value drives the rules.
home.levelsTitle: The UIL Flags, In Plain Words.
home.levelsLead: Class 3 values shown (most of Texas, including Austin). Class 2 schools in the Panhandle and South Plains use lower thresholds.
home.faq1q: Does Flagline replace a WBGT meter?
home.faq1a: No. UIL allows internet based WBGT sources, and Flagline shows two of them. When you have a meter, log its reading. Measured values always drive the live rules.
home.faq2a: The UIL 2026 to 2027 Heat Stress and Athletic Participation Required Plan, the NFHS lightning guidance, and EPA air quality guidance for schools. Every rule links to its source.
home.faq3q: Does it work for marching band?
home.faq3a: Yes. The UIL rule covers band rehearsals too. Flagline applies the break, duration and cooling zone rules to any outdoor activity.
home.faq4a: No names are required. Check-ins can be anonymous or use a jersey number. We keep only what a trainer needs to act.
home.faq5a: Yes, for every school. It needs no hardware and runs on any phone.
home.finalLead: Check your field right now, or run a practice in the demo.
home.footerDisclaimer: Flagline provides planning estimates and workflow support. It is not a medical device and does not replace an athletic trainer, an on-site WBGT instrument, your emergency action plan or emergency services. In an emergency: cool first with cold-water immersion, then call 911.
home.footerAttribution: Weather data: National Weather Service (public domain) and Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0). Air quality: Open-Meteo. WBGT model: Liljegren et al. 2008, ported from ECMWF thermofeel (Apache 2.0).
home.footerMade: Made in Austin, Texas for WarriorHacks 2.0.

emergency.title: Exertional Heat Stroke Protocol
emergency.lead: Use this if an athlete collapses, is confused, acts strangely, or has a very high body temperature.
emergency.step1Body: Remove equipment. Put the whole body in ice water (35 to 58° F) up to the neck. Stir the water and keep adding ice.
emergency.tacoTitle: No Tub? Use The TACO Method
emergency.tacoBody: Lay the athlete on a tarp, fold the sides up, pour in ice and cold water, and keep rocking the tarp so water moves over the body.
emergency.step2Body: Once cooling has started, call 911. If another adult is here, they can call now.
emergency.step3Body: Use a rectal thermometer only. Stop cooling at 101 to 102° F.
emergency.target: Goal: cooling within 30 minutes of collapse.
emergency.survival: Exertional heat stroke has had a 100% survival rate when immediate cooling started within 10 minutes of collapse (UIL).
